clue.text: An entertaining director arranging one more Paris trip

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: arranging puts the letters of 'more Paris' into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A showbusiness boss organises yet another trip to Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: I (one) leads, then 'arranging' shuffles MOREPARIS into MPRESARIO; 'trip' finishes the surface picture of a jaunt to Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario is a theatrical or concert manager who stages entertainments.

clue.text: Gun with hammer up out of use

indicators.note: out of here means the letters for hammer sit outside the word use
in a down clue, up means the word for hammer is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to ram is to hammer or strike hard
taken as written

explanation.surface: A firearm, its hammer cocked, has been taken out of service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hammer' looks like part of the gun; it is the verb. 'up' reverses it in this down entry, and 'out of' wraps that around the word use.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mauser is a German make of rifle and pistol.

clue.text: He rescues deer — mere fluke …

indicators.note: a fluke is a chance accident, so the letters of deer and mere fall together by chance into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone saves a deer by sheer luck, the story continuing in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 4 Down in the surface only; each clue is solved alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A redeemer is a saviour, one who delivers others from danger or sin.

clue.text: deer people found in a foul state

parts.note: a stag is a male deer
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Continuing 3 Down, deer and people are found living in squalor.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation is the condition of still water gone stale and fetid, hence a foul state.

clue.text: Think much of detail

explanation.surface: Value someone for their attention to small points.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem someone is to hold them in high regard; a particular point is a 'respect', as in 'in every respect'.

clue.text: Some are too slow for the city

indicators.note: some here means only part of the words 'are too slow' is taken

explanation.surface: Some people are too sluggish for urban life.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: A fossil men aim to get out

indicators.note: to get out is to escape or break free, so the letters of 'men aim to' break up and reform

explanation.surface: A palaeontologist's find which the diggers are trying to extract.
explanation.definitionFit: An ammonite is the coiled shell fossil of an extinct marine mollusc.

clue.text: Building in which strong beams are essential

definitions.text: Building in which strong beams are essential

parts.words: Building in which strong beams are essential
parts.note: beams read as structural timbers but really mean rays of light shone out to sea

explanation.surface: A structure that depends on sturdy load-bearing timbers.
explanation.walkthrough: Beams suggest joists holding up a roof; the beams that matter are powerful rays guiding ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal tower carries a powerful lamp whose beams warn shipping.

clue.text: Spanish agreement about temporary accommodation for seafood

indicators.note: about means the Spanish word for yes is wrapped around the camp

parts.note: si is Spanish for yes
a camp is temporary lodging such as tents

explanation.surface: A Spanish deal about a campsite somehow ends up concerning fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are langoustines or large prawns, often breaded and fried.

clue.text: Old timers

parts.note: old-timers reads as veterans, but timers are devices that keep time, here ancient ones

explanation.definitionFit: Shadow clocks were among the earliest instruments for telling the hour.

clue.text: Belittle, but bear repeatedly

indicators.note: repeatedly means the word for bear is given twice in a row

parts.note: Pooh is Winnie-the-Pooh, the famous storybook bear

explanation.surface: Disparage, yet a bear keeps coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss something scornfully as unimportant is to scoff at it.

clue.text: A most peculiar flower

parts.note: rum is British slang for very odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: A very strange bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM is old British slang for odd, as in 'a rum business'.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum is a plant with a hooded spathe, such as the lily of that name.

clue.text: Make the connection clear

explanation.surface: Explain plainly how two things link up.
explanation.definitionFit: To join by a hinge or joint is the verb's anatomical sense; speech that is fluent and lucid is the adjective's.

clue.text: Do a number maybe limp into the club?

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: into means the jumbled letters go inside the word for club

parts.note: a cosh is a bludgeon or club

indicators.note: maybe signals that the letters of limp may be rearranged

explanation.surface: Will someone limping into the nightclub perform a routine?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do a number' looks like a performance; 'Do' alone is the definition. A cosh is a short heavy club; 'maybe' jumbles limp before 'into' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve or carry out a task is to get it done.

clue.text: Many a lag without hesitation becomes an idler

indicators.note: without means outside, so the hesitation is put after the word for lag

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
to lag behind is to linger
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Plenty of convicts, quick to act, turn into shirkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lag' looks like a convict, but here it is the verb. 'without' in its old sense of outside puts ER at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A malingerer feigns illness to dodge work, a shirker.

clue.text: Ground for surrounding the queen with attendants

indicators.note: surrounding means the word for attendants goes around the letters for the queen

parts.note: a train is a retinue of attendants
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A reason for the monarch to be encircled by her retinue.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is land considered by its physical features.

clue.text: Offensive character of class appearing before the head

indicators.note: appearing before puts the word for class in front of the word for head

parts.note: rank is social class or standing
a ness is a headland or promontory

explanation.surface: Rude behaviour from someone of standing, brought before the headmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: NESS is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Rankness is a foul or rank quality, such as a smell that offends.

clue.text: High level

parts.note: reads as an amount but means flat land at altitude, or a stage of steady progress

explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is elevated tableland, and also a stable stage after growth.

clue.text: The beastly fighting man who's split a staff up

parts.note: tore means split or ripped

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for staff reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: A brutal soldier who broke a stick in half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly' sounds like brutish, but it means he fights beasts. 'up' turns ROD into DOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A toreador is a bullfighter, one who fights animals.

clue.text: Far from cool

explanation.surface: Anything but chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: Distant means remote in space, and also aloof or reserved in manner.

clue.text: Gratified in accepting nothing can cause conflict

parts.note: content means satisfied or gratified

indicators.note: accepting means the word in takes the letter for nothing inside it

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Being satisfied by having nothing can still lead to strife.
explanation.definitionFit: Contention is dispute or strife between parties.

clue.text: Regret shown about dunderhead being churlish

indicators.note: about means the word for regret goes around the letter from dunderhead

parts.note: to rue is to regret
read as dunder head, the head or first letter of dunder

explanation.surface: Sorrow is expressed over an idiot behaving boorishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dunderhead' is a fool, but split it reads as the head of 'dunder', a D.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude means impolite or ill-mannered, as is a churl.

clue.text: Varieties of aquatic birds — several

explanation.surface: Different kinds of water fowl, a fair number of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Loons are diving water birds of several species; as an old adjective the word means various or sundry.

clue.text: Make a hole in fortune as a knight

parts.note: to lance is to pierce, as with a boil
one's lot is one's fortune or fate

explanation.surface: A knight pierces his fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancelot is a knight of King Arthur's Round Table.

clue.text: Charge a youngster a quarter

parts.note: a lad is a boy
E for east is one of the four compass points or quarters

explanation.surface: Ask a boy to pay twenty-five pence.
explanation.definitionFit: To lade is to load, putting a charge or cargo aboard.

clue.text: Cuts a cross Pole

parts.note: to bridge is to cross over
S is the south pole

explanation.surface: An angry Polish man is snubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' reads as angry and 'Pole' as a Polish man.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge is to shorten, as when cutting a text.

clue.text: Tried, though it's stated otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so the letters of stated are rearranged

explanation.surface: It was attempted, although the record says differently.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste food or drink is to try or sample it.

clue.text: Endeavour to introduce force

parts.note: to enter is to put in or introduce
to prise is to force open

explanation.surface: Try to bring in compulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprise is a bold undertaking or venture.
